papers.title: AI-augmented discovery of autophagy regulators through mechanistic interpretation of multiomics data.
papers.journal: Autophagy
papers.summary: A hybrid AI workflow (LyMOI) combining graph-based deep learning with LLM chain-of-thought reasoning interprets multiomics data, identifying autophagy regulators (Gin4, Elm1, Rvs167, Ste50) and cancer-associated CTSL/FAM98A. Silencing them reduced disulfiram-induced autophagy and tumor growth; DSF plus a CTSL inhibitor potentiated suppression.

papers.title: Multiscale structural evolution of proline-rich protein genes shapes primate salivary defenses.
papers.journal: Molecular biology and evolution
papers.summary: Across 27 primates, salivary proline-rich protein (PRP) genes show lineage-specific duplications/inversions yet rank among top-expressed parotid transcripts. Humans retain high but reduced expression. Exonic tandem repeats and independent colobine histidine-rich trinucleotide repeats correlate with folivory, illustrating how structural and repeat evolution shape salivary defenses.

papers.title: Conserved water molecules shape the pathogenicity of missense variants in human proteins.
papers.journal: Molecular biology and evolution
papers.summary: Conserved water molecules (CWMs) are shown as a determinant of missense variant pathogenicity. Pathogenic variants enrich at CWM sites beyond ligand-binding regions. Molecular dynamics on glucocerebrosidase (GBA1) showed destabilizing one CWM recapitulates L444P-like structural changes, while stabilizing it partially restores wild-type behavior—offering a framework to interpret human genetic variation.

papers.title: No genome-wide correlations and little shared genetic architecture between reproductive life-history traits and estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer risk.
papers.journal: Molecular biology and evolution
papers.summary: Genetic correlations between estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer risk and three reproductive traits (menarche, first birth, children) were low and nonsignificant across biobank and LD-score methods, with only three pleiotropic loci. Little shared genetic architecture between reproductive life-history traits and ER+ breast cancer risk was found in European populations.

papers.title: Streptococcus pyogenes carriage is associated with distinct in vivo transcriptional states but not carrier-specific genotypes.
papers.journal: Cell reports
papers.summary: Analysis of group A Streptococcus before/after pharyngitis treatment found no carrier-specific genotypes and no consistent biofilm or susceptibility differences. However, in vivo transcriptional profiling revealed distinct gene-expression states during acute infection versus post-treatment carriage, though acute-phase profiles did not predict treatment failure. Both bacterial traits and host factors may influence carriage.

papers.title: Menin orchestrates corticogenesis via regulation of chromatin accessibility and activation of EphA4 in late-born neurons.
papers.journal: Cell reports
papers.summary: Menin (MEN1) is essential for corticogenesis, particularly upper-layer neurogenesis. Deficiency disrupts neocortical lamination, neuronal migration, and polarization. Mechanistically, menin regulates chromatin accessibility and H3K4me3 at promoters of developmental genes; EphA4 complementation mitigates polarization defects, linking menin-mediated chromatin regulation to cerebral cortex formation.

papers.title: RNA-binding protein OTUD1 maintains skeletal homeostasis by determining mesenchymal stem cell lineage commitment.
papers.journal: Cell reports
papers.summary: RNA-binding protein OTUD1 controls MSC fate by stabilizing osteogenic transcripts including BMP2 mRNA. Deficiency spares early skeletal development but impairs bone homeostasis during aging and exacerbates osteoporosis models. The N-terminal disordered region mediates RNA binding while the deubiquitinase domain is dispensable, linking mRNA stability to MSC lineage commitment and skeletal aging.

papers.title: Integrated pan-cancer analysis reveals a cancer-associated fibroblast oxidative stress response signature predicting immunotherapy response and prognosis.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: Integrating pan-cancer single-cell data, cancer-associated fibroblasts showed highest oxidative-stress response scores. A fibroblast-derived oxidative-stress signature (FOSR.sig) predicted immunotherapy response with high accuracy and, in a Lasso prognostic model, identified biomarkers across cancers. Top risk gene TFG was mechanistically validated in vitro and in vivo, highlighting CAF oxidative stress as an immunotherapy target.

papers.title: TRIM21 inhibition alleviates acute kidney injury by promoting INTS3-associated DNA damage repair.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: In acute kidney injury, TRIM21 E3 ligase binds INTS3 and promotes its degradation, impairing DNA repair and increasing tubular cell apoptosis. TRIM21 knockout or the small-molecule inhibitor SB33-0223 (targeting its PRYSPRY domain) stabilized INTS3 and reduced ischemia/reperfusion and cisplatin injury, identifying the TRIM21/INTS3 axis as a therapeutic target for AKI.

papers.title: Lactate-dependent regulation of ferroptosis: redox homeostasis, lactylation, and translational perspectives.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: This review examines how lactate bidirectionally regulates ferroptosis through flux, extracellular acidosis, MCT-dependent exchange, and histone/non-histone lactylation. In tumors lactate often supports immunosuppression and ferroptosis resistance, but under certain stress disrupts redox balance. It summarizes translational strategies targeting the lactate-ferroptosis axis while cautioning most evidence remains preclinical.

papers.title: Targeting Runx1 Slows Cyst Growth in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Runx1 expression is upregulated in PKD1 mutant cells via a cAMP-dependent mechanism and drives cyst growth in ADPKD. Pharmacological inhibition (Ro5-3335) slowed cysts in Pkd1 mouse models by blocking AKT-mTOR, MAPK, STAT3 proliferation, suppressing p53 apoptosis, and reducing NF-κB-driven inflammation and TGF-β/Smad2 fibrosis, positioning Runx1 as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Identification of Epigenetic Regulator-Associated Genes in Keloid Disease Through Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomics With RT-qPCR Validation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Machine learning integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identified epigenetic regulator-associated genes in keloid disease; HR and SMYD4 showed significant, consistent differential expression validated by RT-qPCR. Enrichment highlighted metabolic and protein-secretion pathways, altered immune profiles, pseudotime expression of HR in melanocytes, and candidate therapeutic compounds—offering exploratory biomarkers and justification for further epigenetic investigation.

papers.title: Characterization of Ovarian Cell Types and Molecular Signatures in Mauremys reevesii Using Single-Cell Sequencing.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing built an ovarian cell atlas for the Chinese pond turtle Mauremys reevesii, identifying granulosa cells (WNT4, WNT6 markers) and oocytes (UCHL1), with validation by dual-color in situ hybridization. This high-resolution map of ovarian cell types and communication provides a foundation for understanding chelonian reproductive biology and ecology.

papers.title: Circular RNA circLAMC1 Promotes Liver Regeneration by Regulating the miR-138-5p/Gnai2 Axis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: circLAMC1, upregulated after partial hepatectomy, promotes liver regeneration by acting as a sponge for miR-138-5p, which targets Gnai2. Overexpression via AAV9 increased hepatocyte proliferation and liver/body weight ratio after hepatectomy, activating ERK signaling and cell-cycle proteins. circLAMC1 represents a potential regulatory target for promoting liver regeneration after injury.

papers.title: Irisin Restrains Oligodendroglial Ferroptosis to Preserve White Matter After Traumatic Brain Injury via AMPK Activation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Irisin protected against traumatic brain injury white-matter damage by countering XCT-dependent ferroptosis in oligodendrocyte precursor cells. Mechanistically, irisin activated AMPK to suppress cFos, a transcriptional repressor of XCT, via an irisin-cFos-XCT/GPX4 axis. Restoration of irisin preserved white-matter integrity and improved motor and cognitive recovery in a controlled cortical impact model.

papers.title: A Novel Role of DELTEX2 in Maintaining Genomic Stability of Granulosa Cells During Ovarian Aging.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: DELTEX2 (DTX2) maintains genomic stability in granulosa cells during ovarian aging. Aged ovaries show reduced DTX2 and telomere shortening. DTX2 knockdown lowered TERT and increased micronuclei; overexpression mitigated DNA damage, raised TERT, and promoted proliferation under oxidative stress, associated with Notch2 signaling—implicating DTX2 as a potential target for ovarian aging dysfunction.

papers.title: Interleukin-19 Regulates Adipose Tissue Dysfunction in Obesity: Interplay Between Inflammation and Vascularization.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: IL-19 acts as a vascular and immunometabolic protective adipokine in obesity. Il19 knockout mice show reduced adipose vascularization, increased hypoxia/fibrosis/inflammation, and glucose intolerance even on standard diet. Recombinant IL-19 improved vascularization, reduced inflammation, and improved glucose tolerance, partly via IRS2/GLUT-4 upregulation—uncoupling inflammation from angiogenesis to preserve adipose function.

papers.title: Lysosomal Membrane Protein SCARB2 Mediates the Pathogenesis of Diabetic Retinopathy Through the MAPK/ERK/MMP9 Signaling Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: SCARB2 mediates diabetic retinopathy by upregulating VEGFR1/VEGFA under high glucose, promoting endothelial injury and neovascularization via the MAPK/ERK/MMP9 pathway. Elevated SCARB2 was identified by transcriptomics and validated in high-glucose cell and streptozotocin rat models. SCARB2 is proposed as a novel therapeutic target for diabetic retinopathy.

papers.title: Nonlinearities and Switch-Like Behavior in Gene Expression: From Genetics to Biochemistry and Back.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This review links genetic dosage sensitivity (haploinsufficiency of transcription factors and chromatin regulators) to biochemical nonlinearity. It discusses sources of sigmoidal, switch-like gene expression—cooperative binding, chromatin factors, nuclear organization, condensates, epigenetic hysteresis, and network-level nonlinearities—arguing TF/chromatin regulator haploinsufficiency emerges from disruption of diverse molecular architectures rather than a single mechanism.

papers.title: ALKBH5 Positively Regulates BMP2 to Influence Endometrial Decidualization in Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: The m6A demethylase ALKBH5 regulates endometrial decidualization in recurrent spontaneous abortion. ALKBH5 is downregulated in RSA decidua but upregulated during in vitro decidualization. ALKBH5 demethylates BMP2 mRNA, increasing its expression; Bmp2 knockdown reversed pro-decidualization effects of ALKBH5 overexpression. ALKBH5 and BMP2 levels correlate with RSA, suggesting diagnostic and therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Lactylation Modification and Esophageal Cancer: Research Progress From Hypoxia-Induced Metabolic Reprogramming to Immune Escape.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This review covers lactylation in esophageal cancer, where hypoxia-driven glycolysis increases lactate, providing substrate for lysine lactylation of histones (H3K9la, H3K18la, H4K12la) and non-histone proteins. These modifications modulate chromatin, transcription, immune escape, and therapy resistance. Lactylation-linked molecules are explored as potential diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets in esophageal cancer.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Electric Signals Generated at Corneal Wounds.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Corneal wound electric currents are actively regulated, with chloride flux contributing over 80%. Calcium-activated chloride channels (CaCCs) are molecular generators of wound currents; specific blockers reversibly abolish them, while altering intracellular calcium modulates the signal. The currents are energy- and temperature-dependent, linking calcium signaling and chloride channels to wound electric signaling and healing.

papers.title: Unveiling the Immune Mechanisms of Hypertension With Single-Cell Transcriptome-Wide Mendelian Randomization.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Integrating immune-cell eQTLs with Mendelian randomization and colocalization identified 172 causal egenes for hypertension, prioritizing 17. Naive/central-memory CD4, effector CD8, and NK cells were most associated; FNBP4 and PRELID1 link to hypertensive heart disease. Most tier-1/2 targets were druggable with limited predicted on-target side effects, suggesting immune-mediated antihypertensive therapeutic avenues.

papers.title: MBD1-Mediated SDHD Methylation Aggravates Preeclampsia Progression via Triggering Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In preeclampsia, SDHD is downregulated via MBD1-recruited DNMT1 promoter methylation, driving mitochondrial dysfunction in trophoblasts. SDHD overexpression restored mitochondrial function and trophoblast behaviors in hypoxia/reoxygenation cells and reduced rat preeclampsia-like features. This MBD1/DNMT1-SDHD- mitochondrial pathway is implicated in trophoblast dysfunction and preeclampsia progression.

papers.title: Anatomy of a Setback: A Taxonomy of Clinical Trial Failures in Alzheimer's Disease and Strategic Lessons for the Future.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This perspective proposes a taxonomy of Alzheimer's disease clinical trial failures into five categories—wrong target, timing, patient, insufficient target engagement, and wrong endpoint—applied to drugs entered between 2000 and 2025. Failures shifted from target-related toward patient-selection/endpoint issues. Recommendations include biomarker-driven enrichment, mechanism-specific endpoints, and adaptive platforms, suggesting many late-stage AD failures may be structurally predictable.

papers.title: Targeting Mutant Phenylalanine Hydroxylase With Pyrimidine-Triazole Conjugates: A Primary Framework for Candidate Chaperone-Based Strategies in Phenylketonuria.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Pyrimidine-triazole conjugates (Pyr-Tz) were designed as candidate pharmacological chaperones targeting mutant phenylalanine hydroxylase in PKU. Docking showed stronger binding (including mutant R252Q) than sapropterin, with favorable MM-GBSA, ADMET, and drug-likeness. In R252Q cells, Pyr-Tz-2O upregulated PAH and BH4 pathway genes and increased PAH protein, supporting its potential as a PKU therapy.

papers.title: Effects of Fractionated Low Dose Ionizing Radiation on Cellular Senescence in Mouse Lung Tissue.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Fractionated low-dose ionizing radiation increased SA-β-gal activity, senescence-related gene expression, oxidative and DNA damage markers in mouse lung, while raising Nrf2 and MGMT repair gene expression—exceeding compensatory capacity. This dual imbalance in oxidation-antioxidation and DNA-damage repair likely promotes cellular senescence and early radiation-induced lung injury.

papers.title: Wnt3a Downregulation Contributes to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus by Impairing Pancreatic β-Cell Function.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Wnt3a is downregulated in pancreatic tissue and serum of T2DM patients, correlating with metabolic parameters; its rs12401893 GG genotype associates with higher risk. In high-fat-diet and knockout mice, Wnt3a deficiency worsened islet damage and insulin resistance, while recombinant/AAV-mediated Wnt3a improved β-cell function. Wnt3a is proposed as an adjunctive T2DM biomarker and candidate therapeutic target.

papers.title: Macrophage-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Deliver Progranulin to Alleviate Skin Wound Fibrosis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Macrophage-derived progranulin, delivered via extracellular vesicles, suppresses skin wound fibrosis. PGRN was internalized by fibroblasts, upregulating DNAJC3 to inhibit the SRF/α-SMA/CTGF fibrotic pathway. PGRN-enriched EVs accelerated and improved healing in mouse wounds, while EVs from GRN-silenced macrophages were less effective—highlighting macrophage EVs as potential natural therapeutics for fibrotic skin disorders.

papers.title: P53 Competitively Binds P300 to Suppress HIF-1α/TFRC-Mediated Ferroptosis and Promote Doxorubicin Resistance in Breast Cancer.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In doxorubicin-resistant breast cancer, p53 competitively binds p300, limiting p300 availability for HIF-1α and suppressing HIF-1α/TFRC iron uptake and ferroptosis—promoting doxorubicin resistance. p53 knockdown restored HIF-1α/TFRC, enhanced iron uptake and lipid peroxidation, and improved doxorubicin sensitivity. The p53/p300/HIF-1α/TFRC axis is identified as a ferroptosis-regulating route underlying chemoresistance.

papers.title: Shockwave-Induced Myoblast Exosome-Like Vesicles: Emerging Drivers of Muscle Regeneration.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Shockwave treatment of myoblasts produced a rapid, transient increase in exosome-like vesicle concentration at 6 h post-treatment, without changing vesicle size distribution. Ultrastructural analyses confirmed vesicular trafficking and exosome-like secretion. These mechanically induced vesicles may contribute to shockwave-mediated muscle regeneration, positioning exosome release as a potential driver of myogenic and regenerative responses.

papers.title: Targeting TGF-β to Attenuate Ischemia-Reperfusion Associated Muscle Fibrosis and Enhance Regeneration: A Preclinical Study.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In a mouse model combining cardiotoxin injury with transient ischemia-reperfusion, IR impaired myofiber regeneration, increased fibrosis, collagen I/III and TGF-β1, and expanded fibro-adipogenic progenitors. TGF-β-neutralizing antibody reduced skeletal-muscle fibrosis and improved myofiber regeneration after IR, identifying TGF-β-associated FAP activation and collagen deposition as targetable mechanisms of IR-impaired regeneration.

papers.title: Adverse Effects of Carbon Black Nanoparticles on Maternal and Fetal Lungs in Pregnant Mice: Insights From a Metabolomics Perspective.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Prenatal carbon-black nanoparticles (30 and 120 nm) caused severe inflammatory and fibrotic injury in maternal mouse lungs, with 120 nm particles more damaging; both sizes reached fetal lungs without overt histological injury yet elevated oxidative-stress and inflammatory markers. Metabolomics revealed size-specific shifts (histidine vs butanoate/arachidonic acid), indicating fetal molecular dysfunction despite absent morphological damage.

papers.title: Impaired mTOR/SREBP1-Mediated Lipogenesis as a Mechanism of Hepatic Glycogen Accumulation in a Carnivorous Fish Model, Largemouth Bass (Micropterus salmoides).
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In carnivorous largemouth bass, high-carbohydrate diets suppressed the PI3K/AKT1/mTOR axis and nuclear SREBP1, causing hepatic glycogen accumulation instead of lipogenesis; tilapia efficiently activated this axis. Insulin restored AKT1/mTOR/SREBP1, alleviating glycogen overload, while SREBP1 knockdown or mTOR inhibition recapitulated glycogen accumulation—identifying insulin-responsive mTOR/SREBP1 as a key determinant of glucose partitioning in fish.

papers.title: RETRACTION: Up-regulated Mir-192-5p Expression Rescues Cognitive Impairment and Restores Neural Function in Mice With Depression via the Fbln2 -mediated TGF-β1 Signaling Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This FASEB Journal article (Tang et al. 2018, doi 10.1096/fj.201800210rr)—on miR-192-5p, Fbln2, and TGF-β1 in depression—has been retracted. Third-party and publisher investigation found image elements published across multiple articles by different groups, with additional duplication and manipulation, fundamentally compromising confidence in the results. Authors did not respond to the publisher's inquiry.

papers.title: Polygonum cuspidatum Exosome-Like Nanovesicles Alleviate Hypoxic Pulmonary Hypertension by Stabilizing PON1 to Inhibit MAPK-Mediated PASMC Phenotypic Switching.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Polygonum cuspidatum exosome-like nanovesicles alleviated hypoxic pulmonary hypertension in mice, improving pulmonary-artery remodeling and hemodynamics, inhibiting PASMC proliferation/migration, promoting apoptosis, and restoring mitochondrial function. Mechanism involves stabilizing paraoxonase 1 (PON1) to suppress MAPK-pathway activation. PCELNs act through the PON1/MAPK axis, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for HPHT.

papers.title: LCN2-Driven Fibroblast Ferroptosis-Associated Injury Promotes Keratinocyte Proliferation via Lipid Peroxidation Signaling in Psoriasis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In psoriasis, an inflammatory fibroblast subset (IFB1) expands and undergoes ferroptosis-related injury driven by LCN2, which exacerbates lipid peroxidation. Fibroblast-conditioned medium enhanced keratinocyte proliferation; blocking fibroblast ferroptosis or LCN2 knockdown attenuated this. 4-HNE emerged as a mediator of crosstalk, and topical carnosine (a 4-HNE scavenger) alleviated IMQ-induced lesions—implicating a LCN2-driven fibroblast-keratinocyte ferroptosis axis.

papers.title: Protective Effects and Mechanisms of Extracellular Vesicles in Remote Ischemic Preconditioning on Renal Injury Induced by Inflammation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC)-derived extracellular vesicles reduced lipopolysaccharide-induced kidney injury by inhibiting apoptosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in rat and HK-2 models. Proteomics identified tenascin-C as upregulated in RIPC EVs; TNC activated β-catenin and inhibited p53/NF-κB. RIPC also reduced kidney-injury biomarkers in patients undergoing PCNL, suggesting EV-mediated protection against LPS kidney injury.

papers.title: Magnesium Attenuates Renal Senescence and Fibrosis With Reduced DNA Damage Response and H3K4me3 Enrichment at the p16(INK4a) Promoter.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Magnesium attenuated radiation- and ischemia-reperfusion-induced renal damage, DNA damage, cellular senescence, inflammation, cGAS-STING activation, and fibrosis in mice and primary tubular cells. MG2+/MgSO4 reduced p16INK4a transcription and H3K4me3 at its promoter, linking magnesium to reduced DNA-damage response and epigenetic modulation. Results inform strategies targeting fibrosis and senescence-related kidney disease.

papers.title: PCK2 Inhibition Reverses Cisplatin Resistance of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Triggering Ferroptosis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 2 (PCK2) was upregulated in cisplatin-resistant NSCLC and conferred ferroptosis resistance. The compound RGB bound PCK2 at R454, inhibited it, triggered ferroptosis, and restored cisplatin sensitivity in vitro and in vivo. Targeting PCK2 with RGB is proposed as a strategy to overcome chemoresistance in non-small-cell lung cancer.

papers.title: The Src-Family Kinases Hck, Fgr and Lyn Drive Immune Complex-Mediated Glomerulonephritis Through the Syk Tyrosine Kinase.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Src-family kinases Hck, Fgr, and Lyn, elevated in human lupus nephritis, drive immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis. Triple-knockout mice were protected from nephrotoxic serum-induced albuminuria, crescents, and leukocyte infiltration despite normal IgG/complement deposition; bone-marrow transplantation transferred protection. These kinases mediate immune-complex activation of Syk, and their inhibition is suggested as a therapy for glomerulonephritis.

papers.title: ZIP1 Is a Critical DNA Damage-Responsive Zinc Transporter Induced by Bleomycin via the TNFα-NF-κB Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Among ZIP zinc transporters, ZIP1 showed the most prompt induction by the DNA-damaging agent bleomycin in bronchial epithelial cells. Knockdown and overexpression confirmed ZIP1's role in the DNA-damage response. Bleomycin activated TNFα-NF-κB, which bound two sites upstream of SLC39A1 to upregulate ZIP1—helping cells cope with bleomycin-induced DNA damage.

papers.title: Identification of iron and zinc responsive TonB-dependent transporters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
papers.summary: TonB-dependent transporters (TBDTs) are broadly conserved across Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates and prevalent in multidrug-resistant strains. Combining promoter analysis with fluorescent reporters identified 21 iron- and 4 zinc-responsive TBDTs, with metal specificity predicted by promoter regulatory motifs rather than protein homology. The reporter library enables siderophore detection and revealed coordinated metal-acquisition strategies during co-culture with Klebsiella pneumoniae.

papers.title: A drug repurposing screen reveals dopamine signaling as a candidate therapeutic pathway for PIGA-CDG.
papers.journal: PLoS genetics
papers.summary: In a Drosophila eye model of PIGA-CDG, a 1,520-compound repurposing screen found drugs targeting dopamine signaling and cyclooxygenases that improved small-eye phenotype. Pharmacological and genetic inhibition of dopamine D2 receptor signaling and reuptake, plus COX targeting, improved eye and neuro-behavioral phenotypes including seizures and locomotor deficits—pointing to candidate therapies for PIGA-CDG.

papers.title: Dysregulation of CD36 and CPT1A is associated with fatty acid metabolic disorder and cardiomyocyte injury after high-cervical spinal cord injury.
papers.journal: Molecular and cellular biochemistry
papers.summary: After high-cervical spinal cord injury in rats, myocardial ultrastructural injury worsened over 4–48 h with mitochondrial swelling and myofilament disarray. CD36 mRNA and CPT1A protein showed biphasic changes in cardiac tissue, paralleling altered spinal-cord expression. Dysregulation of CD36/CPT1A is associated with myocardial fatty-acid metabolic disturbance, proposing them as targets to prevent SCI-induced myocardial dysfunction.

papers.title: HOXC9 promotes cell proliferation and suppresses mitochondria-dependent apoptosis through the AKT/mTOR pathway in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.journal: Molecular and cellular biochemistry
papers.summary: HOXC9 is overexpressed in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (57.6% vs 22.9% in normal tissue), associated with poorer survival and good diagnostic value (AUC 0.97). HOXC9 promoted proliferation and inhibited mitochondria-dependent apoptosis via AKT/mTOR activation, confirmed by PI3K inhibition and xenografts—supporting HOXC9 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for ESCC.

papers.title: IGF1-IGF1R signaling in tumor-associated macrophages regulates extracellular matrix organization in BRAF inhibitor-targeted melanoma.
papers.journal: Molecular and cellular biochemistry
papers.summary: IGF1-IGF1R signaling in THP-1-derived macrophages regulates extracellular-matrix organization and modulates melanoma sensitivity to the BRAF inhibitor PLX4032. IGF1R deficiency or blockade restrained macrophage polarization; A375 cells pre-co-cultured with IGF1R-deficient macrophages were more sensitive to PLX4032. This reveals a mechanism by which tumor-associated macrophages may contribute to BRAF-inhibitor resistance via ECM remodeling.

papers.title: USP35-mediated NRF2 deubiquitination attenuates experimental cryptorchidism-induced testicular damage and H(2)O(2)-induced apoptosis and oxidative stress in spermatogonia.
papers.journal: Molecular and cellular biochemistry
papers.summary: USP35 is downregulated in experimental cryptorchidism and in H2O2-exposed spermatogonia. Overexpression of USP35 attenuated oxidative damage by inhibiting apoptosis and oxidative stress, interacting with NRF2 and stabilizing it via deubiquitination; impairing NRF2 abolished protection. The USP35-NRF2 axis protects spermatogonia from oxidative injury and is suggested as a therapeutic target for cryptorchidism-induced germ-cell damage.

papers.title: Distinct molecular adaptations underlie convergent phenotypic responses to mannose in normal and metastatic melanocytes.
papers.journal: Molecular and cellular biochemistry
papers.summary: Normal melanocytes and metastatic B16F10 melanoma cells show similar phenotypes to mannose—reduced growth, altered lactate, acidic vesicle accumulation—yet distinct molecular adaptations. Mannose caused modest proteomic change in normal cells but extensive remodeling and phosphoregulation in metastatic cells, with stress/survival/cell-cycle signatures. Cellular context largely determines the adaptive response to mannose-induced metabolic stress in melanoma.

papers.title: Protein O-Mannosyltransferases in Development and Disease: Evolutionary and Functional Insights from Model Organisms.
papers.journal: Glycobiology
papers.summary: This review examines protein O-mannosyltransferases 1/2 (POMT1/2) using Drosophila and zebrafish models, covering dystroglycan-independent substrates including receptor protein tyrosine phosphatases. Model organisms recapitulate multi-tissue dystroglycanopathy defects and reveal compensatory mechanisms. These systems provide a tiered framework to dissect POMT1/2 function and better understand dystroglycanopathies.

papers.title: CD276 promotes lipid metabolic reprogramming and regulates ferroptosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma by upregulating FASN expression via SREBP1.
papers.journal: Human cell
papers.summary: CD276 (immune checkpoint) is overexpressed in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, CD276 activates SREBP1 to upregulate FASN, driving de novo lipogenesis and lipid accumulation while suppressing ferroptosis by increasing GSH and GPX4 activity. Inhibiting CD276 suppressed tumor growth and enhanced ferroptosis-inducer efficacy—proposing a CD276-targeted plus ferroptosis-induction therapy.

papers.title: Gene expression is stable despite widespread cis and trans regulatory divergence in Saccharomyces yeasts.
papers.journal: Genetics
papers.summary: In S. cerevisiae, S. paradoxus and their F1 hybrid, 51.2% of genes showed cis and/or trans regulatory divergence, yet hybrid expression remained largely conserved (81.5% not differing from either parent), with compensatory cis-trans divergence predominating. The cis-diverged LYS2 locus differs in promoter architecture. Regulatory divergence is widespread but buffered, while intron retention is broadly conserved.

papers.title: The serine protease homolog Skanda modulates Toll-Phenoloxidase-mediated immunity in Drosophila.
papers.journal: Genetics
papers.summary: The Drosophila serine protease homolog Skanda, genomically clustered with Hayan and Persephone and induced upon infection, dampens activation of Hayan and, to a lesser extent, Persephone in the Toll-phenoloxidase cascade. Skanda-deficient flies are highly susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus despite normal Toll signaling and melanization, revealing Skanda as a modulator fine-tuning Toll-pathway activity.

papers.title: A screen for adherens junction proteins regulating collective cell migration and testis morphogenesis reveals important roles for the Rab GAP RN-tre and the kinase Par-1.
papers.journal: Molecular biology of the cell
papers.summary: A screen combining proximity proteomics of adherens-junction proteins with Drosophila RNAi in pupal testis identified 22 genes affecting N-cadherin-mediated mesenchymal migration. While E-cadherin supported migration, proteins central to epithelial morphogenesis (Canoe, Polychaetoid, Bazooka) were modestly involved. The kinase Par-1 and Rab GAP RN-tre showed important, distinct roles, providing a resource for junctional regulation of migration.

papers.title: Clearance and secretion of α-synuclein by RTN3L-mediated endoplasmic reticulum autophagy.
papers.journal: Molecular biology of the cell
papers.summary: α-synuclein secretion in human cells is mediated by RTN3L-dependent ER-phagy, working with FIP200 and other autophagy regulators to deliver α-syn to acidic endolysosomes. High α-syn disrupts ER-lysosome traffic, rerouting vesicles to the cell surface; SNARE knockdown blocks secretion. Pathogenic α-syn spread may be a by-product of a misregulated proteostasis or clearance pathway.

papers.title: Age-related molecular and functional remodeling of the choroid plexus in the gray mouse lemur.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: In the gray mouse lemur, aging caused motor-coordination and exploratory declines but preserved working memory. Choroid-plexus transcriptomics identified immune/transport upregulation and communication downregulation, with decreased AQP1 protein (not mRNA) that correlated with motor decline, while NKCC1/TTR were maintained. Aging CP shows selective functional reorganization rather than generalized deterioration, linking CP dysfunction to age-related motor decline.

papers.title: Increasing school attendance and retention in refugee settings: Participatory development of the SchoolLinks intervention.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: This study developed SchoolLinks, an intervention to improve school attendance in Ugandan refugee settings through participatory group model building with caregivers, teachers, and stakeholders. Six strategies emerged: caregiver-teacher meetings, meeting translation, enrolment week with digital data capture, attendance monitoring/incentives, homework clubs, and children walking in groups. Field testing supported the intervention's acceptability, though effectiveness data remain descriptive.

papers.title: Podocyte injury damages podocytes in chimeric organoids.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: In chimeric kidney organoids, immunotoxin injury to targeted podocytes also caused indirect injury in adjacent, non-targeted podocytes—evidenced by reduced podocin staining and podocyte gene expression. This propagation required direct cell-to-cell contact within the same glomerulus and was absent when organoids were cultured separately. Local podocyte interactions may contribute to chronic kidney disease progression.

papers.title: Integrated computational analysis prioritizes candidate targets and pathways linking ochratoxin A exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: An integrated computational workflow linked ochratoxin A exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma, identifying 13 shared targets and prioritizing CYP3A4, KIFC1, AKR1C3, CA2, and TTR with discriminative AUCs of 0.866–0.958. Molecular docking predicted favorable OTA-target interactions; CYP3A4 was evaluated by molecular dynamics. This offers a hypothesis-generating framework for OTA-related metabolic and genomic-instability pathways in HCC.

papers.title: Factors affecting the infestation status of African sugarcane stalk borer (Eldana saccharina Walker) (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae) in Tanzania.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: A Tanzania-wide survey of sugarcane borer Eldana saccharina found infestation highest at high altitude and significantly influenced by season × altitude × crop-age interaction. Internal damage and boring intensity were greater at high/medium altitudes in the rainy season, with bottom stalk most affected; cultivars N41 and N49 and mixed-variety blocks showed higher infestation—guiding pest-management strategies.

papers.title: Metabolic resistance drives cross-resistance in Aedes albopictus to pyriproxyfen and pyrethroid insecticides.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: Thirteen generations of selection produced a highly pyriproxyfen-resistant Aedes albopictus strain (RR50=10.12) with cross-resistance to pyrethroids and significant fitness costs. Resistance was metabolic (p450s, GSTs, carboxylesterases) with no target-site (chs-1/kdr) mutations; synergists largely restored susceptibility. This warns against overreliance on pyriproxyfen-pyrethroid rotation and supports metabolic-resistance monitoring and PBO use in vector control.

papers.title: A descriptive study of early eyelid morphogenesis in a large-scale human embryo collection.
papers.journal: Cells, tissues, organs
papers.summary: Using the Kyoto Collection, this descriptive study mapped early human eyelid morphogenesis. Canthi formed at CS19–21, eyelid retractor and medial palpebral ligament condensations appeared at CS18–20, orbicularis oculi emerged by week 9, eyelid fusion began nasally at CS22 and completed by week 9, and lacrimal canaliculi appeared at CS19—establishing a timeline relevant to congenital eyelid disorders.

papers.title: Ortholog-specific Spatial Expression of Vanins in the Respiratory Tract of Horses.
papers.journal: The journal of histochemistry and cytochemistry : official journal of the Histochemistry Society
papers.summary: Three putative functional equine vanins (evnn1–3) were identified on chromosome 10 with canonical nitrilase domains. Evnn1/2 expressed predominantly in respiratory epithelium while evnn3 localized to submucosal glands; evnn1 and evnn3 were secreted, evnn2 cell-associated, and evnn1 pantetheinase activity confirmed. Distinct airway niches for the evnns may inform research into equine asthma pathogenesis.

papers.title: Whole-exome sequencing in pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy: diagnostic yield and clinical impact in a resource-limited setting.
papers.journal: Neurogenetics
papers.summary: In children with drug-resistant epilepsy at an Indonesian hospital, whole-exome sequencing identified pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 3 of 10 patients (TSC2, CC2D2A, WDFY3) plus two variants of uncertain significance. Variants included missense, nonsense, and frameshift types. WES yielded definitive diagnoses enabling individualized management and genetic counseling in a resource-limited setting.
